cards.explanation: The answer is that the earth is lit up by his glory. The text says it plainly: “…the earth was illuminated by his glory.” This angel comes down from heaven with great authority. I flip on the kitchen light before sunrise and feel pretty important, friends. This angel makes my light switch look like a birthday candle.

The answer is that she has fallen. He says it twice: “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great!” The angel cries it out in a mighty voice. Then he says what she has become: a lair for demons and a haunt for every unclean spirit. I'd say that's a message with some volume behind it.

The answer is True. The angel says, “She has become a lair for demons and a haunt for every unclean spirit, every unclean bird, and every detestable beast.” That's a big change for the great city. The angel isn't describing a place anybody would want to move into.

The word is wealthy. The merchants of the earth “…have grown wealthy from the extravagance of her luxury.” Her luxury was good business for them. I'd say that's a lot of money riding on one city, friends.

The answer is to come out of her. The voice from heaven says, “Come out of her, My people…” It speaks to God's own people. The voice doesn't tell them to wait around and see how it goes. It tells them to leave.
The word is plagues. The voice says to come out “…so that you will not share in her sins or contract any of her plagues.” Coming out is how they avoid both. That's the warning, plain and simple.
The answer is that God remembered them. The voice says, “…God has remembered her iniquities.” Her sins are piled up to heaven, and God has not let them slip by. Iniquities means wrongdoing, friends.

The answer is double. The voice says, “pay her back double for what she has done…” and goes on, “mix her a double portion in her own cup.” Double is the number, and it shows up twice in the same verse. I'd call that a voice making sure you heard it.

The answer is that she says she sits as queen and will never see grief. In her heart she says, “I sit as queen; I am not a widow and will never see grief.” That's a lot of confidence for a city whose sins are piled up to heaven. I think she sounds awfully sure of herself.

The answer is in one day. The voice says, “Therefore her plagues will come in one day—death and grief and famine…” She said she'd never see grief, and grief shows up in a single day. After all that bragging, the turnaround is quick. The voice also says she will be consumed by fire.
The answer is False. The voice says, “…mighty is the Lord God who judges her.” The kings aren't the judges here. They were immoral with her, and later they weep over her.

The answer is that they will weep and wail. The text says the kings “…will weep and wail at the sight of the smoke rising from the fire that consumes her.” They lived in luxury with her. Now they watch the smoke and weep. I think this one is heavy, friends.
The answer is at a distance. The kings “…will stand at a distance…” in fear of her torment. They watch from far off. Then they cry out, “Woe, woe to the great city, the mighty city of Babylon!”
The answer is False. The kings cry out, “Woe, woe to the great city, the mighty city of Babylon! For in a single hour your judgment has come.” One hour is the word. No long years anywhere.

The answer is that no one is left to buy their cargo. The text gives the reason: “…because there is no one left to buy their cargo…” The merchants weep and mourn over her. Gold, silver, pearls, fine linen and more are on their list. Without a buyer, none of it moves.
The answer is False. The merchants say, “all your luxury and splendor have vanished, never to be seen again.” Vanished means gone, friends. And never again means no someday.

The answer is fine linen and purple and scarlet. The merchants cry, “Woe, woe to the great city, clothed in fine linen and purple and scarlet, adorned with gold and precious stones and pearls!” It's a picture of her at her fanciest. That's the picture they paint in their cry.
The answer is, “What city was ever like this great city?” At the sight of the smoke, the shipmasters and sailors exclaim it. I think they're still in shock.

The word is enriched. They cry, “…where all who had ships on the sea were enriched by her wealth!” Everyone who had ships on the sea was enriched by her wealth. Then they cry that in a single hour she has been destroyed.

The answer is True. The merchants “…will stand at a distance, in fear of her torment.” (verse 15). The shipmasters, passengers and sailors “…will stand at a distance…” too (verse 17). The kings do the same (verse 10).

The answer is rejoice over her. The call is, “Rejoice over her, O heaven, and you saints and apostles and prophets…” The kings, merchants and sailors mourn her. Heaven and the saints and apostles and prophets get a different message, friends. They're told to rejoice.

The word is judgment. The text says, “…because God has pronounced for you His judgment against her.” God is the one who pronounces it. The saints and apostles and prophets are told to rejoice because of it.

The answer is that he casts it into the sea. The mighty angel “…picked up a stone the size of a great millstone and cast it into the sea…” Then he says what it stands for: “With such violence the great city of Babylon will be cast down, never to be seen again.” He throws it, and then he explains it.

The answer is True. The mighty angel says, “With such violence the great city of Babylon will be cast down, never to be seen again.” The stone he threw into the sea goes along with the words. Never to be seen again is the line to hold on to, friends.
The answer is False. The angel says, “Nor will any craftsmen of any trade be found in you again…” That covers any trade at all. The workshops are empty.

The answer is the voices of a bride and bridegroom. The angel says, “…the voices of a bride and bridegroom will never call out in you again.” It's a happy sound, and it goes quiet in her for good. I think that's one of the saddest lines on the list.
The word is deceived. The angel says, “…because all the nations were deceived by your sorcery.” The nations were deceived by her sorcery, friends. That's what the angel says.

The answer is the blood of prophets and saints. The text says, “And there was found in her the blood of prophets and saints, and of all who had been slain on the earth.” I think this is a heavy one, friends. It's not a line to hurry past. And the story isn't over, because there's more still to come.
